newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee firms, central bank watches.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee firms, central bank watches.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India kept to the sidelines on Monday, allowing the rupee to edge firmer against the dollar both in the spot and forward markets, dealers said.
The spot market continued to see large inflows stemming from dollar sales by Indian exporters as well as remittances from foreign investors, dealers said.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) did not buy dollars on Monday, helping the spot rupee to close the day at 35.85/86, firming from the day's opening level of 35.86/87, they said.
The central bank has been a persistent buyer of dollars recently to stop the rupee appreciating.
The six month annualised forward premium closed at 6.25 percent, down from the previous close of 6.58 percent.
The Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI), India's leading term-lending bank, was receiving premia for near-term forward dollar transactions, dealers said.
"The market was little cautious today because of IDBI," said a forward dealer at a foreign bank.
"But only the IDBI was receiving today," he said.
Dealers said importers were not covering their forward dollar requirements because a steady rupee did not show any sign of depreciating against the dollar in the near term.
"I feel importers should cover their risk now as the premia could rise next week," Arun Dobey, vice president and director (forex) at Bank of America told Reuters on Monday.
"The current levels are good for importers," Dobey said.
He said overnight call rates were expected to spurt next week because of an outflow of about 40.0 billion rupees from the banking system towards payment of advance tax by companies.
RBI said India's foreign currency reserves rose to $20.09 billion on March 6, up from $19.69 billion on February 28.
"It's very comfortable and is good enough to cover about half of India's annual imports," said a treasury manager at a foreign bank in Bombay.
The current reserves level augured well for India's plans to make the rupee convertible on the capital account, he said.
The Indian government announced last month-end the RBI had been asked to prepare a "road map" to make the rupee fully convertible on the capital account.
